subject.title: Port OpenClawTray.FunctionalUI to Reactor to stop hand-maintaining bespoke UI primitives

question: Should the Windows tray adopt Microsoft.UI.Reactor as its supported UI architecture and dependency, beginning with a bounded leaf-screen spike, or continue investing in the in-repository FunctionalUI framework?
rationale: Source inspection can establish that the migration is absent and technically motivated, but it cannot choose the repository’s long-term UI dependency, maintenance, and migration strategy.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded spike
options.body: Port one low-coupling screen alongside FunctionalUI and require dependency, testing, accessibility, selection, and runtime proof before approving further migration.

options.title: Retain FunctionalUI
options.body: Keep the current framework and define a narrower policy for adding tested primitives only when concrete product needs arise.

options.title: Approve the full migration
options.body: Commit to an incremental Reactor migration now, with one ownership seam per pull request and FunctionalUI removal only after all consumers and invariants move.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded spike
recommendation.body: Port one low-coupling screen alongside FunctionalUI and require dependency, testing, accessibility, selection, and runtime proof before approving further migration.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice governs the tray’s long-term architecture and external dependency strategy rather than one individual primitive implementation.
